answer.text:
Human gate at in-progress -> complete by default, movable to the front by pre-approval. Archive is mechanical.
Default: the agent drives draft -> in-progress and works until every claim has a receipt; only a human advances to complete. Pre-approval: a human may write `approved-by: <name> @ <sha>` on the change, the sha pinning the claims section. The pre-transition hook to complete accepts an agent completion when the approval is present and the claims are unchanged since the sha; any claim added, replaced or removed after approval stales it and the gate is back at the end. The gate is never absent; the human chooses per change whether to verify intent up front or the result at the end. complete -> archived runs the fold hook with no judgement. "Ready for review" is derived (in-progress, all claims receipted, validate clean), not a status. review-work is the agent's advisory self-review before declaring receipts complete; output shown, not stored. The human reviews the change document plus the diff since in-progress. The agent never writes approved-by; the Stop hook flags an approval field written during the agent's own session. PR merge, if the project has one, is orthogonal to the document gate.

A false positive is waived where it occurs, as a line under the claim with a reason; validate counts waivers as an info finding alongside [intent] claims so the ratio stays visible. Contract mutation and a flagged re-pin are warnings at validate and Stop; at the completion gate they invalidate approved-by, returning the gate to the human, who sees the flag when completing.

answer.text:
Release 1 (thin slice): pack with spec, change and decision types, core testing dictum and the fix/chore/refactor dictum; binary with receipt-resolves-and-fresh at complete, fold by id at archive, cross-governs bound plus static pending-test read at Stop, validate continuous, ten-line CI job; skills: entry and change. Acceptance demo in hydra, five steps. Release 2 and later enumerated below.
Release 1 demo (acceptance test, in hydra): (1) lazyspec init --template from the lemma repo; (2) one evergreen spec for the reopen cascade, Intent plus governs; (3) a change with two claims, one [intent], built, with @ref receipts to real cargo test symbols; (4) complete blocked while a receipt is missing, passes the human gate once added, archive hook writes spec lines by id; (5) governed-code edit with no change open shows the receipt stale and re-pin clears it; an edit across two governs areas is flagged at Stop.

Release 2 (the rest of the settled v1 design, on evidence from release 1):
- Types: idea (open -> promoted | dropped) and bug (open -> closed, reproduction claim, violates link, two close paths); convention and dictum templates with tagged-claim rules whose receipt is the enforcer.
- Skills: shape (ideate, design -> hydra, specify router over idea | hydra tree | prompt, plan, decide, triage), verify (test, conform = review-work three stages at the completion gate, audit filing bugs/ideas), maintain (reconcile, housekeep, configure), operate (ship, orchestrate sequential dispatch, resume).
- Guardrail catalogue remainder at validate: two in-flight changes touching one claim id; fold target does not resolve; [intent] count and waiver count as info; verified-by / approved-by stale by sha; evergreen spec without governs; spec without a rationale link; contract mutation naming affected claims and specs.
- Pre-transition draft -> in-progress: Intent present, at least one claim, fold targets resolve (agent self-advances).
- Completion gate: approved-by required for agent-invoked completion; contract mutation and flagged re-pin revoke approved-by.
- re-pin subcommand hardening: refused when the symbol no longer resolves; flagged after a receipt-file change with no matching claim change.
- Stop additions: approved-by written this session; contract mutation on session-touched receipt files.
- Severity policy: per-instance in-document waivers with a reason, counted as info; no config table.
- verified-by human sign-off receipts; [intent] ratio reporting.
- Optional stack dictums directory (testing-web etc.) pruned by the setup step.
- UserPromptSubmit convention preamble injection.
- Second adopter: the lemma repo self-hosts.

Release 3 and later, each gated on a concrete need shown in dogfooding: jev advisory grading of [intent] claims and change-document review at the completion gate (optional, no API key = no-op); JUnit XML report ingestion as a second evidence kind; PreToolUse edit gate bounding edits to the in-progress document's governs; per-claim implementation @ref; intra-change parallelism via claim ownership written by orchestrate; GitHub issue sync for bugs; lazyspec adoption and migration from the rfc/story/iteration chain; version coherence across pack, plugin and binary.

v1-scope.question: What is the minimum first release: which of pack, skills, hooks, binary, jev are in, and what is the first end-to-end demo that proves it?

answer.rationale: prompting cannot scope context by code locality, cannot know when context has decayed, cannot prove intent was met, and does not keep rationale in the repo. No existing framework has a graph, code anchoring or a decay signal. Value scales with codebase age and session count. User: hooks are crucial, verification must be built into the system.
answer.text: Scoped, decaying, verifiable context for a memoryless agent, as typed nodes anchored to code -- with verification built into the graph and enforced by hooks. Hooks are not a convenience layer; they are how "no unverified completion" becomes true.

value-proposition.question: What is the utility over existing frameworks and over just prompting Claude with a good CLAUDE.md?

answer.rationale: synthesis of the four children
answer.text: Verification is in the graph, not a runner. Claims are tagged list items with stable ids; receipts are @ref lines to test symbols, pinned by sha and stale on drift; the codebase runs the tests and CI owns pass/fail. Hooks: validate warns, pre-transition blocks, Stop bounds the diff and re-validates touched docs, CI runs the same binary. Untestable claims are marked [intent] or signed off by a human; jev is a trial grader for those.

verification.question: How is verification built into the system without the framework running tests: what is a claim, what is evidence, how is the link (receipt) represented, how does the framework learn pass/fail and freshness, and at which hook points is it enforced?

version-coherence.question: With three install channels, how is a pack/skills/binary version mismatch detected: a version stamp in .lazyspec.toml the binary checks on every hook, a validate-hook finding, or not at all in v1?

answer.rationale: one birthplace for specs regardless of how much thinking preceded it; rationale link is automatic when a tree exists; no change needs to exist before a capability can be described; matches spec-audience (agent-authored, human-reviewed, brief, rationale-bearing). rejected.why_not: spec inherits one change framing, narrower than the capability

answer.text:
Spec minted only by the specify workflow, a router skill over three inputs: promoted idea, hydra tree, or prompt.
The agent authors Intent, constraints and non-goals at the highest authorship level the input supports (generate from a tree, co-write from an idea or prompt); the human reviews; the spec goes active with an empty Behaviour. The tree or idea is linked as rationale. Claims arrive only by change archive. Whether a hydra tree is required before specify is decided under interview-stage.

wf-creating-specs.question: How are specs created: hydra interview first, then co-write/generate from the tree; agent drafts from a prompt; or the human writes and the agent reviews? What input does a spec start from?

answer.rationale: prompting cannot be designed as one thing; the framework treats a prompt as an instance of one of these workflows, each with its own planning and verification policy. Set is provisional and amendable.
answer.text: Twenty-four prompt workflows in six groups. Orientation: explain, orient, investigate, review. Shaping: ideate, design, specify, plan, decide, triage. Changing code: build, fix, chore, refactor, spike. Verifying: test, conform, audit. Maintaining: reconcile, housekeep, configure. Operating: ship, orchestrate, resume. Orientation and resume are always free.

wf-prompting.question: How does the developer prompt Claude? Free prompt with the convention preamble injected; always through /lazy against a document; or a hook that rewrites or blocks prompts without a document anchor?

answer.rationale: tracks bugs durably in the graph without a second work unit; reuses the receipt model instead of adding a lifecycle; keeps the fix policy true (simple fix needs no plan); the delta-off-a-bug trigger is the escalation trigger already decided, not a new rule; spec stays writable only by the archive hook

rejected.why_not: triage state not in the graph, validate cannot surface open bugs against a claim; conflicts with dt-inventory
repeals the fix policy, two documents per one-line fix, breaks friction-per-interaction definition of lightweight

rejected.option: bug is a change with kind
rejected.why_not: bug: unfixed bugs pollute work-in-flight as draft changes, wontfix has no natural state
a second in-flight unit competing with change

answer.text:
Thin bug record, tracked, never driven; closes by its own regression receipt or by a spawned change resolving it.
A bug is a point-in-time type (open -> closed, close reason fixed | wontfix). It carries one reproduction claim (tagged list item) and links the spec claim id it violates. Two close paths. Direct fix: the regression test is an @ref receipt on the bug; pre-transition to closed requires the receipt to resolve, or a wontfix reason. Delta: when the violated claim itself was wrong, or the fix trips the existing escalation trigger (cross-governs / complex / risky), the bug spawns a change that resolves it; the change carries the replaced claim and its receipt; the bug closes when the change completes. The bug never amends a spec; only the archive hook writes specs. A closed bug's receipt is graph evidence against the spec claim. Tracker (GitHub issues) sync is out of scope for v1.

wf-reporting-bugs.question: How do bugs enter: a bug document type (this repo has one: reported/triaged/in-progress/fixed/wontfix), GitHub issues synced, or a failing test? How does a bug link to the spec it violates, and does a bug ever amend the spec?

answer.rationale: same intake pattern as bug: thin, point-in-time, never driven, in the lazyspec graph so links, validate age-staleness and the TUI/web views see it. Hydra is not a dependency concern (user owns it) but its states (open/answered/cauterised) only map to open/promoted/dropped rather than fit, an unpromoted idea is a head with nothing to ask, and a backlog tree holding every interview becomes the whole design history in one file

rejected.option: ideas as hydra heads in a backlog tree
rejected.why_not: richer drop rationale and in-place promotion, but invisible to the lazyspec graph, two intake surfaces, and cross-tree promotion is the same seam as a link anyway
drafts become the backlog, dropped has no state, vague idea has no fold target
contradicts dt-inventory and the bug precedent

answer.text:
Thin idea type in the lazyspec graph: open -> promoted | dropped. Intent only; promoted links what it became (a change or a hydra tree).
No claims, no receipts. Dropped carries a reason. Promotion to an interview mints a fresh hydra tree and the idea record links it; promotion straight to a change links the change. Bug and idea are the two intake types, same shape; bug adds a reproduction claim, a violates link and a receipt path. Revisit only if hydra grows a backlog mode with non-question heads and cross-tree promotion.

wf-tracking-ideas.question: Where do ideas live before they are specs: an idea/proposal document type, hydra heads, GitHub issues, a backlog file, or nowhere (an idea is a draft RFC or it is nothing)?

answer.rationale: settled by oracle-per-workflow; jev and review-work remain open under their own heads
answer.text: Correctness is verified by the codebase's own tests and checks, run by pre-commit and CI, never by the framework. The framework requires receipts: an @ref from each AC to a resolving test symbol before complete. review-work and jev are advisory review, not gates; their exact role is decided under the jev heads.

wf-verifying.question: How is correctness verified: mechanised acceptance criteria (dom-test), tests referenced as contracts, jev conformance grading, review-work skill, human review? Which are required and which are advisory?

answer.rationale: taken from lazyspec_workflow_binary_spec.md section 4; position-independent
answer.text: Human edits never break the flow. Drift is detected from changed files against governs. Later agent work in an affected area may start immediately and must resolve only the drift relevant to its task before completing; unrelated drift stays visibly stale. Automation-first: mechanical repairs (renames, moves) where existing lazyspec facilities support them; semantic discrepancies presented for review scoped to the claims relied on. Never re-pin to silence a finding.

wf-volatility.question: How is codebase volatility managed: governs globs + reviewed sha + staleness bands surface drift today. What triggers spec re-review, who does it, and what blocks while a governed spec is stale?

answer.rationale: matches dev-workflow: human decisions on the shaping track, agent evidence on the delivery track; every hook decided under verification sits on a delivery transition; children slot cleanly (interview-stage = shaping, plan-gate and review-stage = delivery transitions, test-harness = what delivery consumes)

rejected.why_not: small changes visibly skip four stages and the skip becomes the argument
specs and decisions become side effects of changes; hydra has no slot

answer.text:
Two tracks joined at the spec. Shaping (human-paced): idea -> optional interview -> specify -> decision. Delivery (agent-paced, hook-enforced): change draft -> in-progress -> complete -> archived.
A change targets a spec; shaping produces specs and decisions, delivery produces claims and receipts that fold into specs at archive. Bugs enter delivery directly (regression receipt on the bug) or via a spawned change. Artefacts: idea record; hydra tree; spec shell (Intent only); decision record; change with claims; code+tests+receipts; receipted change; spec lines rewritten by id.

workflow.question: Given the six activities, what is the end-to-end stage sequence from idea to merged code, and what artefact does each stage produce and consume?

answer.rationale: settled by oracle-per-workflow: classification was the heavy part and is gone
answer.text: Nobody classifies. The framework reads only two structural signals: is there an in-progress document, and does the diff cross governs areas. The fix/chore/refactor/spike distinction lives in a dictum and in the agent's judgement; misjudgement is caught by the codebase's checks and by the cross-governs flag, not by a label.

workflow-classification.question: Who decides which workflow a prompt is (agent self-classifies, human declares, hook infers from the diff), and what stops an agent calling a risky change a chore? Is misclassification caught at the prompt, at the edit, or by the oracle at completion?

intent: Design a metaframework, in a separate repo from lazyspec, that wraps lazyspec for LLM-driven development: a lazyspec pack, a set of skills, an opinionated workflow, possibly a hooks binary, enforced guardrails/validation/verification, and possibly jev integration. Decide what it is, what it is not, how it relates to lazyspec's packs/hooks/governs, and how it reconciles the "specs should express intent and reference executable contracts rather than duplicate code" thesis, drawing on the spec-judge, dom-test and hydra experiments. Output: a design settled enough to write the founding RFC/README for the new repo.
